messages:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed multiple README snippets in the quickstart that are out of sync with the Node SDK v2. New hires keep pasting them into sample apps and hitting 401s or strange retry behavior.
Ken: ugh. Which snippet specifically?
Maya: the auth example. README shows `process.env.REDWOOD_KEY` and `new Redwood({ apiKey: ... })`, but our Node SDK now uses `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` and `Redwood.fromEnv()` convenience factory. People copy/paste the old constructor and get a missing-header 401.
Sara: also saw the Python sample still calling `Client(api_key='...')` instead of `RedwoodClient.from_env()` — parity drift across languages.
Alex: and there's a sneaky one in the sample app Dockerfile: it sets ENV REDWOOD_KEY=... so even if devs set REDWOOD_API_KEY locally, containerized example is wrong.
Maya: exact reproduction steps I gave to TSE: clone sample-app, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, build, run, POST /chat returns 401. swap env name in Dockerfile and it works.
Ken: oof. Is this breaking any tests? docs CI should catch env-var mismatches but it only runs link checks.
Sara: we don't have unit tests for the copy/pasteable snippets. I can add a tiny smoke test that runs the readme node example with a fake token to check it emits the expected client init code path.
Alex: About retry behavior — the README shows a snippet adding retry: `{retries: 3}` to the client. That used to be global retry for all requests, but runtime changed to idempotent-only by default. Folks copy the snippet, expect POST to be retried on 5xx and get duplicate side effects. We need to call this out.
Maya: suggested wording for README: "The SDK's retry default retries only idempotent requests. For non-idempotent operations (POST), wrap logic with idempotency keys or opt-in to non-idempotent retry with caution."
Ken: can we include the short code patch inline? e.g. in Node:```js
// recommended: explicit idempotency key for POST
const client = Redwood.fromEnv();
await client.chat.create({
  messages: [...],
  headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': uuidv4() }
});
``` and for Python:```py
# use from_env and pass idempotency header for non-idempotent calls
client = RedwoodClient.from_env()
client.chat.create(messages=..., headers={"Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())})
```
Sara: +1. Also add a short note in the sample-app README about the container env var (Dockerfile) using REDWOOD_API_KEY.
Maya: I've drafted a tiny PR to fix the examples and update the copy text: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1423 — includes: change env var names, replace direct constructors with from_env helpers, add idempotency header examples, and a follow-up smoke test.
DocsBot: PR 1423 submitted by @maya — CI checks pending :github: .
Ken: can someone from eng-runtime/SDK give a quick :eyes: on the retry wording? We need to be careful describing "default" behavior across SDK versions.
Alex: I can review. Quick note: we changed default in Node v2.1.0 and Python v1.8. Defaults are now conservative (idempotent-only). Add a version note in the README snippet like `(Node >= v2.1.0, Python >= v1.8.0)`.
Sara: I'll add the smoke test as part of the PR and update the sample-app Dockerfile in a separate commit.
Maya: thanks — can we also update the onboarding quickstart doc to point new users at `sdk-compat.md` so they know about these cross-lang diffs? New hires keep assuming parity.
Ken: good call. Once PR is green let's merge and backport a tiny changelog entry so customer-facing docs indicate the fix.
Alex: ack — will review today.
Maya: thanks all. I'll ping again after tests are green. :rocket:
